text: Define Channel<T> backpressure: bounded queue depth per channel, sender behaviour when the receiver is slow (block-as-Operation, fail, drop-by-policy), and expose queue depth via os inspect.
Bound kernel-object consumption per ResourceDomain (handles, tasks, channels, memory objects, outstanding Operations) as a pids-controller equivalent, with typed exhaustion errors.
Define the memory-charging rule for a MemoryObject whose ownership moves between ResourceDomains (charge follows owner; a borrow never double-charges) and test budget enforcement across a transfer.
Specify component panic and abort semantics: a Rust panic aborts only that component; stack overflow and OOM abort are reported as typed exit causes to the supervisor; no unwinding crosses the ABI.
Define a typed file and directory change-notification Operation (inotify/fanotify replacement) and its Linux-personality bridge, required by IDEs at V1.
Define mapping of a Capability<File> into a MemoryObject: coherence with Write Operations, an msync equivalent, and interaction with copy-on-write snapshots.
Define the durability contract of Write and StorageTransaction (the point at which data is power-loss safe) and prove it with a fault-injected power-cut test on NVMe.
Retain overlayfs, FUSE, user namespaces and seccomp-bpf in the fork and verify them from the Linux personality at V1 (Chromium sandbox, Flatpak/bubblewrap and podman depend on them).
Provide a ptrace-equivalent for the Linux personality (gdb, strace, Wine debugging, Crashpad) gated by an explicit debug capability.
Establish the kernel developer workflow for the fork: QEMU gdbstub, kgdb, early console, crash-dump analysis with drgn, documented in one page and exercised in CI.
Retain and run kselftests for every retained subsystem in the nightly test matrix.
Retain hardware watchdog, softlockup, hung-task and NMI detection and wire them to the service supervisor and the crash-capture path.
Decide eBPF's native role (tracing substrate, sched_ext, network policy) and whether the Linux personality exposes bpf() beyond a CAP_BPF-equivalent capability.
Steer interrupt affinity as a ResourceDomain CPU-policy input for LowLatency domains and measure the effect on the audio benchmark.

Publish a microarchitectural side-channel position statement: what isolation the capability model claims, which shared resources (glyph atlas, shared MemoryObjects, SMT siblings) are cross-domain channels, and which mitigations are on by default.
Provide a safe-mode session: when the shell or compositor exhausts its restart budget, the supervisor starts a minimal recovery shell with settings, log export and os restore.

Define the behaviour of running applications when their package is replaced by a new generation (old objects stay mapped, restart prompt, deferred activation) and test that no running component observes a mixed-version tree.
Key persistent capability grants on package identity plus publisher rather than content hash so grants survive application updates, and revoke them on publisher change.
Provide the system CA trust store as a typed object with per-application pinning and enterprise-CA enrolment, consumed by native TLS and mirrored into the personalities' certificate stores.
Provide remote shell access for developers at V1 (sshd via the Linux personality, with a later decision on a native typed remote shell) with the network-listen capability explicit.
Implement display power management (DPMS, panel self-refresh, idle dim and off) tied to idle, lock and lid state.
Implement audio device hot-plug and default-device switching (headphone jack, HDMI/DP audio, USB), a per-application volume mixer, and Bluetooth codec selection.
Provide an echo-cancellation and noise-suppression pipeline for conferencing, shared with the media framework.
Support hardware cursor and overlay planes, direct scanout, and tearing/immediate presentation for fullscreen games and HDR video.
Support hybrid-graphics laptops (iGPU plus dGPU, render offload, mux switching) across the compositor and both personalities.
Support DisplayPort MST and daisy-chained docks in the multi-monitor hot-plug test.
Define a Steam runtime sub-corpus (pressure-vessel, gamescope, user namespaces, 32-bit multilib, /dev/input via udev, SDL game-controller evdev) with its own scenario scripts.
Decide whether ia32 (32-bit) emulation is retained in the fork before any syscall-pruning work, since Steam and many Windows titles depend on it.
Package Windows runtime redistributables (VC++ runtimes, .NET, WebView2, legacy DirectX) as per-prefix dependencies rather than runtime downloads.
Bound Windows background services, scheduled tasks and autostart entries inside a prefix by the owning component's lifecycle.
Support per-application personality version pinning (multiple Wine/Proton builds coexisting via package multi-versioning) surfaced in native UI.
Provide a native profiler: sampling CPU and GPU profiles attributed to Task and Component rather than threads, flame graphs by TaskGroup, exportable with traces.
Publish interface design guidelines for IDL authors (naming, error taxonomy, async and stream patterns, capability-passing idioms) reviewed before the first Layer 2 interface freezes.
Provide storage quotas per user and per ResourceDomain with settings UI, distinct from content-store garbage collection.
Provide disk health: TRIM/discard policy, SMART monitoring, checksum-scrub error reporting UX, and filesystem repair from the recovery environment.
Provide encrypted, snapshot-based, scheduled user-data backup to external or network targets as the counterpart of machine-to-machine restore.
Declare sensor support per device class (ambient-light auto-brightness, lid and tablet-mode switches, accelerometer rotation) as in or out of scope for 1.0.
Declare casting (Miracast/Chromecast/AirPlay), NFC, WWAN/eSIM and MIDI/pro-audio as post-1.0 so they appear in the published non-goal list.
Accept a Windows-personality scoping decision at V0 as the only V0 Windows deliverable.
Provide offline on-device documentation (os help and a man-page equivalent inside the Linux personality).
Decide that kernel live-patching is a non-goal: system generations plus reboot are the update model.
Assign input-stack ownership explicitly: device enablement (libinput/evdev/HID, keyboard layouts, gestures) in HW, routing and focus in UIP.
Provide a firmware update service (fwupd-class) whose updates are recorded as system-history events.
Provide desktop search and indexing as a background-intent component over storage capabilities.
Decide that Rust std support for native targets lives at Layer 3 as a compatibility crate over the native SDK; no Layer 1 entry point may be justified by std's POSIX-shaped APIs.
Decide that V0 boots Linux init from a retained initramfs and starts native components beside it; a native init replaces it at V0.5.
Decide that X11 primary selection is emulated inside the Wayland/X11 bridge and never crosses into the native clipboard.
Publish the threat model before capability, security and boot designs are fixed; every CAP/SEC/BOOT decision cites the threats it addresses.
Build the photodiode or high-speed-camera input-to-photon measurement rig on the reference desktop before the V0.5 compositor benchmarks.
Procure power meters and establish the energy-measurement methodology before the V1 battery gates.
Procure an HDR reference display and colorimeter for the V2 HDR gates.
Procure and rack the reference machines per tier with remote power, console and capture, and a scheduler for soak runs.
Provide a KVM-based VM manager as a capability-scoped component with typed VirtualMachine objects.
Provide guest tools and seamless guest-window integration for Windows and Linux guests.
Publish JakeOS guest images for common hypervisors so developers can onboard in a VM.
Provide the compatibility-triage flow that offers the VM fallback for software the personalities cannot run.
Decide the media pipeline architecture: sandboxed codec components exchanging MemoryObjects, hardware decode via VA-API or Vulkan Video, and the camera service model.
Package codecs as isolated components with per-codec capability sets and licensing metadata.
Provide a camera service minting Capability<Camera> with a persistent in-use indicator.
Provide screen-recording encode through the explicit screen-capture capability.
Add regression-versus-previous-milestone and publish-only target kinds to the benchmark register so milestone gates can express 'no regression greater than N%' without restating numbers.
Add a compatibility-corpus register (C-IDs) defining L0–L5 and W1–W3 with sizes, scenario scripts, rating scales and per-milestone thresholds.
Add a threat register (T-IDs) that CAP, SEC and BOOT decisions cite.
Add an invariants register (I-IDs) for standing rules, each with the lint or test task that enforces it.
Accept the accessibility tree model decision before the UI protocol's Layer 2 freeze, and emit role/name/state metadata from every widget at V0.5.
Register the input-method protocol shape (preedit, commit, surrounding text) as a Layer 2 surface before the UI protocol freezes, even though IME engines ship at V2.
Reserve signature, signer and trust-policy fields in the package manifest before the first immutable install.
Accept the capability grant taxonomy decision (one-time, session, persistent, revocable-by-user) before the package capability-request schema.
Bring Wine up on the Linux personality and run the Wine test suite nightly in CI as non-gated V1 work; define the W1 corpus and per-title scenario harness.
Provide the system image builder and scripted install used by developers before an end-user installer exists.
Define supervision semantics (restart budgets, rebind protocol, readiness reporting) that the V0.5 compositor-restart gate depends on.
